subject: Post-demo: Finlytics pilot engine recommendations and tradeoffs
messages:

Subject: Re: Demo recap — Finlytics pilot

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning — the demo clarified a lot. A few quick notes from our side so we're aligned before the pilot kickoff: 

- Primary KPI: answer latency p95 <= 350ms for 512-token replies (interactive analyst UI).
- Cost target: target <= $0.0015/token averaged across mixed traffic (short prompts + medium replies).
- Quality: accuracy on our benchmark set (NICE-50) should be within 6% of our current LLM baseline on entity extraction and instruction-following.

We liked the idea of a two-tier strategy: fast low-cost fallback for chatty traffic, and higher-quality engine for complex queries. Please send your recommended shortlist, the prompt set you used for the scorecard, and any perf/price numbers so we can validate with procurement.

Also, Priya from procurement will want a rough SOW and a path for SOC2 evidence.

Best,
Evan

--
Evan Stone
Director, Platform Engineering | Finlytics
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Demo recap — Finlytics pilot

Evan — thanks for the clear summary and the target metrics. Short version up front: attached is a compact recommendation (3 engines) with the prompt pack and our internal benchmark CSV. Below I summarize the tradeoffs and the suggested pilot path.

Recommended shortlist (why these three):
- Redwood-Base-13B (int8): best balance of quality → recommended as the primary engine for the pilot. Solid instruction-following and entity extraction on NICE-50; expected p95 ≈ 320–380ms depending on qps and routing. Cost estimate: mid-range.
- Lumen-7B-quant (4-bit): faster and cheaper fallback for high concurrency. Lower absolute accuracy on edge cases but substantially lower per-token cost — good for conversational chatter and routing. Expected p95 ≈ 200–280ms.
- OpenDelta-2.7B (optimized): ultra-low-cost candidate for bulk embedding-like work and short replies where precision tolerance is higher. p95 ≈ 120–200ms; quality drops in long-form context.

Why a 2-tier routing policy: route short/conversational traffic to Lumen-7B-quant or OpenDelta-2.7B, and route flagged or high-risk queries (entity extraction, compliance prompts) to Redwood-Base-13B. This keeps average cost down while meeting quality when it matters.

Attachments included: prompt pack (finlytics-prompt-pack-v1.txt) and the raw CSV with our NICE-50 runs (benchmark-results-0722.csv). The CSV contains per-prompt exact-match/F1, latency med/p95, and per-token cost estimates used in the summary.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Procurement path: Priya — we'll share a one-page SOW + SOC2 checklist and an initial quote (attached redwood-reco-quote-2026-07.pdf).
2) Pilot configuration: 2-week smoke + 4-week production pilot. We propose baseline traffic routing and 3 guardrail experiments (prefix caching, KV cache warmup, and quantized fallback tuning).
3) Technical sync: Karthik to run a 60-minute bench session with your infra (we'll bring the prompt pack and a minimal test harness).

I copied Ben for commercial alignment. If that looks good I'll drop a calendar invite for Friday for the bench session.

Thanks,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 13:30:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — Finlytics pilot (bench results + notes)

Evan — quick note with the practical numbers from our local bench run using your prompt pack (attached). Full dashboard link: https://app.redwood.internal/perf/dashboard/finlytics-0722

Bench highlights (NICE-50 subset, 512-token generation budget):
- Redwood-Base-13B (int8): median lat 210ms, p95 360ms; NICE-50 F1 = 0.86; est cost ~ $0.0013/token at pilot qps (with shared prefix cache).
- Lumen-7B-quant (4-bit): median lat 140ms, p95 250ms; NICE-50 F1 = 0.80; est cost ~ $0.00055/token.
- OpenDelta-2.7B: median lat 85ms, p95 160ms; NICE-50 F1 = 0.72; est cost ~ $0.00028/token.

Operational notes and risks: 
- Regression risk: certain extraction prompts (long tables, mixed language) see a ~6–10% hit on OpenDelta; recommend guardrail tests before routing any extraction work there.
- Cache warmup: 40% latency variance between cold and warmed prefix during our run; plan a brief staged warmup during pilot ramp.
- Quality regressions: we recommend a small eval harness (5–10 prompts) to run nightly against a golden set — we'll open a shared results sheet and alert on delta > 3% F1.

Pilot tuning knobs we propose to test (each mapped to a success metric):
- Smart route threshold: automatically promote to Redwood-Base-13B when confidence < 0.75 (measured by internal scoring).
- Aggressive prefix caching: reduces generated-token cost by ~12% for repeat workflows.
- Quant fallback hysteresis: only fall back to lower-capacity engines when queueing delay > 150ms to avoid quality oscillations.

I'll host the bench artifacts in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/finlytics/prompt-pack-v1 and upload the raw CSV (benchmark-results-0722.csv). If you want, we can also snapshot model logs for a short audit.

--
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
